newsitem.title: USA: "Men In Black" zaps U.S. box office records.
newsitem.headline: "Men In Black" zaps U.S. box office records.

text.p: "Men in Black," an alien comedy starring Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones, crunched the competition as it opened at the top of the holiday box office, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.
The picture earned about $84 million for the five-day Wednesday to Sunday period, which includes Tuesday night previews of $4.8 million, said Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.

Its Friday-to-Sunday total of $51 million is the biggest non-sequel opening ever, and the third-biggest overall behind "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" and "Batman Forever," the studio said. It's also the biggest opener in Sony history.

Last weekend's No. 1, "Face/Off," starring Nicolas Cage and John Travolta, earned $16.5 million during the three days, a modest drop of 29 percent from the previous weekend. Its 10-day total stands at $52.06 million. Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc., released the action thriller.

Third place went to Walt Disney Co.'s animated musical "Hercules" with $12.4 million for the three days, a 38 percent drop from last weekend when it opened in wide release. Its gross to date is $50.26 million.

"Men in Black," one of the summer's most heralded movies, features Smith and Jones as top secret federal agents who monitor extraterrestrial life forms living in disguise on Earth. The spoof was directed by Barry Sonnenfeld ("Get Shorty").

According to Robert Levin, president of marketing at Sony Pictures, the studio opted to downplay the film's tongue-in-cheek nature, which could have confused moviegoers, and instead focus on its "cool" aspects.

"If we ever went to that area where it seemed like it was a spoof and it was just over the top filmmaking, I think we would have gone wrong," Levin told Reuters. "But I think the idea that it was a very cool, hip execution really got through to people, and I think that was important."
He said exit polls showed that almost 80 percent of people said they would definitely recommend the movie, and this would ensure its box office strength in coming weeks.
"Men in Black" earned an average of $16,887 from 3,020 screens for the three-day period, followed by "Face/Off" with $6,257 per screen.

"My Best Friend's Wedding" was unchanged at fourth on the box office list with $11.0 million in its third weekend. The Julia Roberts romantic comedy fell 27 percent from last weekend, the smallest dip in the top 10, and averaged $4,926 per screen, the third-highest. Its total is $69.5 million. The film is released by Sony's TriStar Pictures studio.

"Batman & Robin" fell two places to fifth in its third weekend with $8.6 million, bringing its total to $91.3 million. Its 45 percent drop was the biggest in the top 10, and it averaged a meager $2,923 per screen. The movie is released by Warner Bros. a unit of Time Warner Inc.
The top 10 contained two other new entries, each aimed at totally different demographics, but both faring poorly.

"Out to Sea," a maritime comedy starring Walter Matthau and Jack Lemmon, opened in sixth with $5.6 million. "Wild America," a road movie starring teen heartthrob Jonathan Taylor Thomas, opened in ninth with $1.8 million.
Twentieth Century Fox, a unit of News Corp., released "Out to Sea," while Warner Bros. released "Wild America."
